result:
I graded `submissions/s1.json` and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. You got 2 correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong | The model doesn't open the booking system. It writes a request naming `check_calendar` with its arguments, and the program runs it. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against a repeating loop. |
| q4 | wrong | The answer is 4 model calls, not 1. The model can't run tools. Each tool request ends a call, and the program calls the model again with the result. |
| q5 | partial | "It sends it back to the model" is the *what*. You left out the *why*: the model hasn't seen the result yet, so it needs it to choose its next step or write the final answer. |
| q6 | partial | Choosing a tool from its name and description is right. The model doesn't remember earlier sessions on its own, though. The program has to supply any memory. |

The mistake behind q2 and q4 is the same one: believing the model runs or opens tools itself. The q6 memory claim is a separate one, and it leads into our next topic. I also added a learning record (`learning-records/0003-model-requests-program-runs.md`) and updated `NOTES.md`. `s2` is still ungraded.

**Next step:** redraw your laser-cutter trace with two columns, "model" and "program". Mark every model call, then retake the quiz.

Do you want me to grade `s2` next to see whether the model-versus-program split has settled?
